## What is Bayes' Theorem?

:::{.theorem data-title="Bayes' Theorem"}

Bayes' theorem states that for events $A$ and $B$ with $\mathbb{P}(B)\neq 0$ then the conditional probability of $A$ given $B$ can be computed with $$\mathbb{P}(A|B)=\frac{\mathbb{P}(B|A)\mathbb{P}(A)}{\mathbb{P}(B)}.$$

:::

Bayes' Theorem is a fundamental result in Bayesian inference where is is used
to express the posterior distribution in terms of the prior distribution and
the sampling distribution
$$
p(\theta|y)=\frac{p(\theta,y)}{p(y)}=\frac{p(\theta)p(y|\theta)}{p(y)}\propto p(\theta)p(y|\theta).
$$
